configs.description: The lacing bar as Middle Atlantic lists LBP-1A, one bar of the pack of 10.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the cut sheet and the SKU page say the bar provides fixed tie points and give no slot, count or place along it. The slots drawn are estimates read from a small photograph. A dimensioned drawing would settle them. No cable is told which slot to use.
gaps.wanted: a Middle Atlantic dimensioned drawing that marks the slots a cable is tied to

gaps.note: the cut sheet gives "Mounting Points 2" and neither the size nor the place of the holes. The ear holes drawn are estimates read from a small photograph. A dimensioned drawing would settle them, with the hole pattern against the rack unit.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the bar

gaps.note: the cut sheet gives 0.5 in for the height and 0.5 in for the depth of an L-shaped bar. It does not say which is the face and which the leg, nor the sheet gauge. The L drawn at each end uses a stand-in thickness and the photograph's reading of which side is which. The 3D L is two raised plates; the kit has no single profile for an L.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing, or an end-on photograph, of the bar

gaps.note: the bar is 12.7 high and takes one 44.45 rack unit in this model, which is an estimate. No document says where in the unit it sits. None says whether the ears span more than one.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the bar fitted to a rail

gaps.note: no document gives the weight of one LBP-1A or of its pack of 10. The series page lists 2.5 lb for the whole series. The environmental profile gives 2510 g with packaging for a different reference product. Neither is this bar's.
gaps.wanted: a Middle Atlantic specification that gives the weight of LBP-1A

gaps.note: the documents held here say nothing of screws or other fixings for the two mounting points.
gaps.wanted: the part's installation sheet or parts list

attrs.note: datasheet - the material and finish are the series page's "steel construction with black powder coat finish". Rectangular bars of aluminium are another style. The colour is its Color row, Black.

chassis.note: datasheet - 19 in (482.6 mm) wide, 0.5 in (12.7 mm) high and 0.5 in (12.7 mm) deep. These are the cut sheet's Width, Height and Depth rows (page 1). The height is far under the 44.45 of the rack unit it takes. The cut sheet does not say which 0.5 in figure is the bar's face. The other is the projection from the rail face; see the `cross-section` gap. The maker's 12.7 by 12.7 is kept as stated. A raised plate stands out of its face, so the drawn L is 1.5 mm taller and 1.5 mm deeper than the stated box. Its width is the stated width.

color.note: estimated - "Black". The photograph's 4317 dark pixels average RGB 45, 55, 58, a near-black. Dark pixels are those whose three channels sum under 330, counted in the bar's box. The shade drawn is this library's render of black, the same as its other black lacing bar and managers.

ears.note: estimated - an ear 20 mm long beyond the web at each end, a tab of the top leg 8 mm wide. Its obround hole is 10 by 3 mm, from 3 to 13 mm from the end. The ears read about 21 and 19 mm in the photograph and are drawn alike. Same perspective fit and scale along the bar as the slots. Good to about 6 mm. The ears continue the top leg, so the top and bottom show them; the front and rear show them edge-on, with no hole. In 3D each ear continues the leg beyond the web. It is a frame of four raised rects round the hole, with the leg's `out`, level with the leg's top face. The painted ear and hole stay in the 2D drawing.

front.note: estimated - the bar's web as 442.6 by 12.7 between the ears, with its ten slots. The slots are 3 mm high, 6 mm below the web's top edge. Across the bar the scale is the web's printed 12.7 mm over its height on the 4x crop of the photograph. That height is 50 px at x 300 (y 342 to 392) and 44.5 px at x 1600: 0.254 to 0.285 mm/px. The slots are painted vents; the 2D face paints a hole dark, as the library does everywhere. The web is a raised plate standing out 1.5 mm. It starts one gauge above the top edge and is one gauge taller. Without that the slabs touch only along an edge and leave a groove.

guides.note: datasheet - none. The SKU page says the bar provides "fixed tie points" and gives no count or place. The slots are drawn as decor, and the format has no tie point on a bar (`tie-points` gap).

left.note: estimated - the end as an L of two 1.5 mm strips, the web at the front and the leg along the top. The thickness is a stand-in and the sheet does not say which 0.5 in is the projection. The right is the same. In 3D the end shows only as the end faces of the two slabs, with no closed end cap. The end-on view reads as an L only if you know to look for one. It draws less than a photograph would.

method.note: FIGURES FROM A SPECIFICATION TABLE AND ONE SMALL PHOTOGRAPH. The maker's generated cut sheet for LBP-1A (page 1) and its SKU page state the depth, height and width, the offset and its angle. They also state the style, the two mounting points and the pack of 10. The cut sheet is one embedded picture of the whole page, 1588 by 2094 px. The bar's photograph is a strip about 433 by 92 px in it. NO MAKER DOCUMENT HELD HERE HOLDS A DIMENSIONED DRAWING. The slots and ears are read from the photograph and every figure for them is estimated (`slots` and `ears` entries). Only the overall size is the maker's. The series page's weight and the environmental profile's mass belong to another reference product (see the `weight` gap).

mount.note: estimated - the cut sheet says "Mounting Points 2" and "Component Type Horizontal". The SKU page says to choose an offset bar by the distance from the rear of the equipment to the rack rail. The photograph shows a flat ear with one small hole at each end. So the bar is taken to be fixed to the rail at its ends. It is a `rack-face` part, as the library's other lacing bar and managers are. At what height inside the unit it sits, and which rack unit it spans, are not stated.

rear.note: estimated - the back of the same web. The slots pass through and the layout is symmetric along the bar, so it shows what the front shows. No document shows the bar from behind.

shell.note: estimated - `sheet`: the series page says steel construction and the photograph shows a thin L-section strip. The section is not dimensioned, so the end faces draw it at the stand-in thickness below. The web is the face toward the front, tall and vertical. The leg is horizontal at the top and runs back from the web's top edge. The maker's sheet gives 0.5 in for each and does not say which is which. The photograph decides it: a tall dark face toward the viewer, with the narrow leg behind and above it.

slots.note: estimated - ten slots on the web and ten on the top leg. Both rows were counted twice on the photograph, by eye on 4x crops and by brightness runs. A perspective fit to the ten centres gave a pitch of about 41 mm and a length of 30 mm. The first centre is 57 mm from the end and the row is drawn centred. The scale along the bar is the ear tips spanning 482.6 mm. Good to about 3 mm. The slots do not show in 3D: a painted vent shows neither dark nor open on a sheet device. They are drawn in the 2D faces only. Opening them would mean splitting each plate into raised rects round them.

thickness.note: estimated - 1.5, the stand-in the library's other sheet cable managers use; no Middle Atlantic document states a gauge. It is the source of the gauge. Every `out` on a base plate and every rect size that adds the gauge restates it, and all must equal it. Nothing checks this in the kit. A test for this device asserts it. Nothing checks which leg is the web, the sealed corner, the ear level, or that each ear frame matches its painted hole.

top.note: estimated - the top leg 12.7 deep between the ears, with ten slots at the web's positions, and the two ears with their holes. The rear edge is at the top of the drawing, as the viewer draws a top face. The bottom is the same plate seen from below. Across the bar the scale is the web's printed 12.7 mm over its apparent height (0.249 mm/px at the ears, fitted from the front). The ear is 30 px (8 mm) and its hole 12 px (3 mm) on the 4x crop at x 90. The leg slot is a stand-in: 6 mm wide, 6 mm from the rear edge, half the leg's 16 px depth (y 326 to 342). The leg is a raised plate standing out 1.5 mm. The rear, bottom and end faces carry neither `sink` nor `out`, so they build nothing in 3D.
